Watch the Trailer for M. Night Shyamalan's REMAIN: "From Warner Bros. Pictures, Remain, starring Jake Gyllenhaal, is an unprecedented collaboration between two of the world’s most creative minds: best-selling author Nicholas Sparks, and visionary filmmaker M. Night Shyamalan.

When reclusive architect Tate Gordon moves to small coastal town to complete his latest project, he encounters an alluring young woman who pulls him out of his shell, and into the center of a deadly mystery that hangs over the town.

Gyllenhaal stars alongside Phoebe Dynevor, Ashley Walters, Julie Hagerty and Jay O. Sanders.

Shyamalan directs from his own screenplay, story by Shyamalan and Sparks.  The film is produced by Shyamalan, Ashwin Rajan, Marc Bienstock and Theresa Park, with Sparks executive producing.

Joining Shyamalan behind the camera are director of photography Adolpho Veloso, production designer Sam Lisenco, editor Noëmi Preiswerk, costume designer Caroline Duncan, casting director Douglas Aibel, music supervisor Gabe Hilfer and composer James Newton Howard.

Warner Bros. Pictures Presents a Blinding Edge Pictures Production, an M. Night Shyamalan Film, Remain, in theaters across North America February 5, 2027, and internationally beginning 3 February 2027, distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures."

Joe Bob Briggs and Picturehouse Announce New Genre Label Coney Island Pictures, Basket Case Remake Announced: "Coney Island Pictures, a horror-focused production and distribution company, was launched today by legendary indie distributor and producer Bob Berney and Joe Bob Briggs, the late-night movie host best known for three long-running series on cable and streaming services.

“I’ve known Bob since the eighties,” said Briggs, “when the two of us were rooming together at the Cannes Film Festival to save money and collaborating on weird film festivals at the only real arthouse in Dallas. Bob went off to Hollywood, distributed the two most successful indie films in history, marketed movies worth a billion in box office, many of them winning Academy Awards, and developed friendships with the top directors in the business, while I was writing books about exploitation movies and hosting ‘The Night Evelyn Came Out of the Grave’ at 1 a.m. on cable. Our two worlds eventually collided through what I call the Horror Renaissance of 2016. Bob’s friend Guillermo del Toro won the Academy Award, and AMC Networks launched the Shudder streaming service, where I would spend almost a decade putting the trivia embedded in the back of my brain to work.”

Picturehouse, Berney’s innovative distribution and marketing company, is set to distribute Coney Island’s projects worldwide.

“I’ve known Joe Bob since I owned the Inwood Theater and he was the film critic at the Dallas Times Herald,” says Berney, CEO of Picturehouse. “Together, in the early ’90s, we screened both classic and unknown genre films with special guest stars and tributes. The status of horror has been greatly elevated in today’s marketplace, and Coney Island Pictures is uniquely situated to acquire and produce a new generation of films with the added advantage of being able to talk directly to the fans of Joe Bob Briggs. It’s something we’ve always wanted to do and the time is right.”

In addition to Berney and Briggs, who will serve as Co-CEOs of the new company, long-time Picturehouse marketing maven Jeanne R. Berney will serve as Head of Marketing for the new endeavor, and former Explorers Club media executive Austin Raywood will serve as Head of Production.

Coney Island has several projects in development, including a dark horror comedy, a new version of a classic horror paperback, and a reimagining of the 1981 cult horror classic ‘Basket Case’ in collaboration with original Director Frank Henenlotter.

Anthony Sneed, Henenlotter’s longtime creative partner and protégé, will helm the new adaptation for Coney Island.

Said Briggs: “I sponsored the world premiere of the original ‘Basket Case’ at the Highway 183 Drive-In in Irving, Texas. Bob helped me promote it with the World Drive-In Movie Festival. Now, decades later, we’re working with its original creator, Frank Henenlotter. Because every generation needs a ‘Basket Case!’""

ScareScore Partners with Broadway Horror Hit Paranormal Activity to Expand its Audience Measurement Platform From Screen to Stage: "ScareScore, the biometric entertainment platform that turns an audience’s physical reactions into a personal score, today announced a partnership with Paranormal Activity, the smash-hit, sold-out, critically acclaimed production currently playing on Broadway at the August Wilson Theatre. Beginning on November 19 and continuing through the production’s final February 28, 2027 performance, theatergoers wearing a compatible smartwatch can opt-in, free to measure their body’s responses to the show’s scares, then compare their ScareScore with friends after the curtain falls. The partnership marks ScareScore’s first move from the screen to the stage, demonstrating that the most telling review of a live experience is the one your body writes while it’s happening. 

“A review tells you what someone thought after the show – ScareScore shows you what your body did during it,” said Chris Anastas, Founder and CEO of ScareScore. “Your watch reads your heart rate and movement, we match those reactions to the moments that caused them, and when the curtain comes down, you get a score that shows how hard the experience hit you.” 

James and Lou move from Chicago to London to escape their past, but they soon discover that places aren’t haunted, people are… With an original story inspired by the film franchise, Paranormal Activity reimagines the modern ghost story with an intimacy that only live theatre can provide. Written by Levi Holloway and directed by Felix Barrett Paranormal Activity stars Cher Álvarez as Lou, Travis A. Knight as James, Shannon Cochran as Carolanne, and Eva Kaminsky as Etheline Cotgrave. 

“Paranormal Activity is built on tension that you can cut with a knife: those long, silent stretches where an entire theater is holding its breath – and that’s exactly what ScareScore was made to capture, and there’s no bigger stage for that kind of experience than Broadway,” said JP Ouellette, Co-Founder of ScareScore and producer of the Sundance drama Mass. “For a live theater production like Paranormal Activity, ScareScore represents a new way to connect with an audience and to understand exactly where a story lands. Part of what makes this so exciting for us is that it doesn’t stop at Broadway. The same idea works anywhere people gather to feel something together: a movie premiere, a series finale watch party, a haunted attraction, a concert – every live experience is about to have a scoreboard, and the audience gets to keep the score.” 

Tapping the power of ScareScore requires theatergoers download the free ScareScore app on an iPhone paired with an Apple Watch, or an Android phone paired with a Wear OS smartwatch, and op-in before the show and complete the required setup with their account. During the performance, the phone stays silent and the watch goes dark in Movie Mode, so nothing lights up, buzzes, or distracts the cast or the people in the next seat, and no one can check or game a score mid-show. Users can pause the session during intermission.After the curtain call, each guest’s ScareScore is revealed, showing which moments hit the hardest and how their reaction stacks up against friend and the rest of the night’s audience. 

Paranormal Activity is playing a strictly limited engagement on Broadway through February 28, 2027 only. Tickets are available at paranormalbroadway.com and at the August Wilson Theatre box office."
